newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese shares seen steadying after 3 pct drop.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese shares seen steadying after 3 pct drop.

text.p: Losses in Portuguese shares are likely to be limited to the three percent drop in the index seen at the opening, provided Wall Street does not repeat Friday's plunge, analysts said on Monday.

They said buy orders had emerged after the PSI20 index fell three percent to reach a low of 8,006.48 points shortly after the opening. By 1015 GMT the index had staged a tentative recovery to stand at 8,115.32, down 142.86 points.
The PSI20 has risen more than 56 percent so far this year.

"The index has risen so much already, it's natural that our guideline should now come from foreign markets," said Joaquim Reis of brokerage Central de Investimentos. "But with three percent knocked off the index we're seeing buy orders and prices are off lows."
"If New York opens higher, we could recover almost everything we've lost today or even close stronger," he added.
Analysts said some investors were taking advantage of Friday's 3.11 percent tumble in the Dow Jones -- the biggest fall since the stock market crash of 1987 -- to take profits.

"Conditions in Portugal will remain positive for as long as the Bundesbank doesn't raise German interest rates," said Jose Freire at Espirito Santo Research. "So long as that doesn't happen the Bank of Portugal still has room to lower its rates."
The Bundesbank sets its repo rate tomorrow and its council meeting is due on Thursday.

Seven out of eight analysts polled by Reuters said the Bank of Portugal was unlikely to change its money market rates when they come up for review later today. All eight agreed that the central bank still had room to lower rates.
Analysts said the continuing lower trend in interest rates and strong economic fundamentals meant the domestic market remained attractive to investors.
Total volume on the Lisbon bourse was more than five billion escudos with banks the biggest losers, registering losses of around five percent, following recent strong gains.
BCP was down 78 escudos at 3,600 on volume of 148,970 shares, but up from an opening 3,560.
BPSM fell 55 escudos to 2,612 with 233,150 shares traded after opening at 2,580.
PSI20 August futures were down 127 points at 8,113.
